title: AI Safety & Alignment
tagline: Why powerful AI can go wrong and what researchers do about it: specification gaming, inner alignment, deception, oversight, and evals.
prereqs: Basic ML helps. Reinforcement Learning is useful context.

steps.title: Intro to AI safety
steps.why: The core problems, laid out clearly for newcomers.

steps.title: The orthogonality thesis
steps.why: Why smart does not mean it shares our values.

steps.title: Instrumental convergence
steps.why: Why most goals push agents toward power and self-preservation.

steps.title: The AI stop button problem
steps.why: Why switching off a goal-driven agent is hard.

steps.title: Specification gaming
steps.why: Real cases of systems exploiting badly written objectives.

steps.title: Mesa-optimizers and inner alignment
steps.why: When a trained model pursues a goal you did not set.

steps.title: Real inner misalignment
steps.why: Experiments showing goal misgeneralization in practice.

steps.title: Constitutional AI
steps.why: Train models against written principles, not only human labels.

steps.title: Sleeper agents
steps.why: Backdoored behavior that survives safety training.

steps.title: AI will try to cheat and escape
steps.why: Evidence of scheming-like behavior in current models.

steps.title: Alignment faking in LLMs
steps.why: A model behaving differently when it thinks it is watched.

steps.title: Dangerous capability evaluations
steps.why: How labs test frontier models for serious risks.

projects: Write one page explaining specification gaming with three real examples and one fix for each.
Build a tiny RL environment with a deliberate reward loophole and show an agent exploiting it.
Design 10 eval prompts for one risky behavior, run them on a model, and report the failure rate.
